calls.reason: The only evidence is Bloomberg's estimate that OpenAI made up about 70% of Microsoft's AI sales. That covers one supplier, with no market-wide denominator for either share.
Gemini's 1 billion monthly users and Ramp's business adoption data are not comparable paying-customer or growth measures. Nothing classifies the labs' customers as mostly AI startups.
Oracle's prospectus gives the original tranche terms, but no complete October 6 yield set was found. The added-interest total cannot be calculated either way.
Anthropic's S-1 shows about $265.6B in fixed commitments, but no spending breakdown shows whether either lab could cut total costs. The claim is largely a judgement.
PIMCO's event study found surprise AI debt deals did not significantly raise ten-year yields and said most of the rise reflected expected policy rates. That supports 'not the big reason'.
Anthropic's S-1 shows positive first-half operating cash flow, against the cash-flow part. Its small property and equipment figure leaves the main point about few owned assets unsettled.
